title: The ridge from the loading dock, 1994
logline: The loading dock at the last shift's end, dusk, and above the ridge beyond the yard, the glow — drawn in 1994 for the first time. It was there before the strip. The sequence says so and doesn't explain.

panels.composition: The mill's loading dock at dusk, 1994, the last stacks of cedar, a forklift, and beyond the yard's fence the ridge, with the glow above its trees — the same warmth the Sundays found in 2009, here fifteen years earlier, in the mill's own last light. Spotting heavy; the glow the one soft thing.

image.prompt: a single full comic page with no borders, heavy black ink spotting in a 1990s zine style, a mill loading dock at dusk with stacked cedar and a forklift and beyond a fence a forested ridge with a soft warm glow above its trees, the glow the only soft element, no words
image.notes: The glow in 1994. Before the strip. Not explained.

art.line: spare, knowing; economy of line; Era I's black spotting back on purpose in the mill run
